summary: The pre-vote-disabled receipt separated the two gates that the earlier negative result had left entangled, and the result is a clean attribution rather than a weakened one. All twelve trials produced what they were built to force — the isolated voter sat at terms three to five against a leader at two or three, so a real higher-term candidacy was alive throughout — and yet not one confirmation overlapped a competing election: comparison 0 came back violated and complete with all twelve trials as valid witnesses, no trial saw a competing leader during the window, and the confirmations ended at the leader's lease in every case (47-59ms, seventeen to twenty each) with the leader stepping down each time. Read against the earlier run, where pre-vote kept the isolated voter at the leader's own term, the two receipts say: pre-vote prevents an isolated node from raising its term at all, and it is the peers' refusal to vote while they still have the leader in view — released only when their own heartbeat timers expire — that keeps the separation once a candidacy exists. I corrected the behaviour entry under its existing id with that changed premise and named its recorded use, marked the question answered, and the mixed-timer finding keeps its place as the only path into the defect, now for the precise reason that only a node whose own timer is shorter than the leader's lease can get ahead of it. With that, the record is complete: three execution-grounded findings — the startup replay that blocks NewRaft, the nonvoter acknowledgement that satisfies VerifyLeader's voter quorum and, under per-node timers, can accompany committed state the confirming leader never applied, and the membership change that installs a voter immediately and can strand a single-voter cluster — plus four refuted suspicions and one excluded cause, each with the evidence and the limits that bound it, and every registered question answered. One item is left for a subsequent turn if the run continues: the correction's affected-use hook is reported by validation as adding a gap to the adverse-phase question, and since it is created by this same batch I cannot answer it here.
